skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest radiograph with circled or highlighted pulmonary opacities to determine the specific diagnosis and anatomical distribution.
steps: Identify the radiographic pattern of the opacity within the highlighted region, specifically looking for hazy increased attenuation that does not obscure underlying vessels (ground-glass opacity).

Determine the precise anatomical location of the finding by referencing visible bony landmarks (e.g., ribs, clavicle, hemidiaphragm) to confirm laterality (right vs. left) and vertical zone (apex, mid, or base).

Correlate the combination of ground-glass morphology and unilateral basal distribution with early-stage viral pneumonitis patterns, while excluding diagnoses characterized by bilateral involvement, contralateral findings, or traumatic etiologies.
